current.text: He has played in preseason and is reported healthy. He says he has no minutes restriction.
Experts expect early-season minutes limits from coach Rick Carlisle, plus some missed games and a ramp-up period. One note says this could last a month or two.
He is expected to sit some back-to-backs early, or play only one game of each. Tony expects about 30 minutes in games that are not part of a back-to-back.
Experts expect rust to lower his usage and efficiency early in the season. One speaker worries that his two-point percentage could drop from about 59 to 57 after the Achilles injury.
Some experts worry about compensation injuries after the Achilles tear.
Experts expect him to reach full minutes and his best level later in the season. The estimates range from January to February, and all of them put it before the fantasy playoffs.
Experts say rank 10 on Yahoo is too early, even in category leagues. They put his fair range at 14 to 20: the middle of round 2 is fine, and the end of round 1 is acceptable.
In an auction mock, Josh would not pay more than 35 USD for him. He sold for 36 USD, which Josh called a little high.
Indiana is projected as a playoff team, with about 46 to 48 wins.
With a season ending March 28, Indiana plays 3, 4 and 3 games in the fantasy playoff weeks. The note calls that not ideal. The team has 15 back-to-backs.

durable.text: He tore his Achilles in the June 2025 NBA Finals and missed all of the 2025-26 season. He also had a case of shingles.
His assists are elite, and he is always a threat to lead the league in assists. Draft him early if you want assists.
He is not a high scorer or a high-usage player. He is an assist source more than a points source, so drafting him early leans a team toward punting points.
He is a great shooter. In his last full season he made just under 40% of his threes.
His steals and FG% have been good, and two-point finishing is a strength.
He picks apart confused defenses and commits very few turnovers for his playmaking load.
Experts say he is not a top 10 player in Yahoo points leagues, even at his best. Points rankings underrate him for category leagues like ours.
How he plays shapes the fantasy value of every other Pacer.
Coach Rick Carlisle keeps players' minutes low even when they are healthy, and he rests players on back-to-backs.

note: His average cost is 48.6 USD on Yahoo and 40.1 USD on ESPN, and our league did not draft him last season. Experts cap him near 35 USD and rank him 14 to 20, so let others pay the Yahoo price. He fits assist-heavy builds that can give up some points (about 9.4 AST, 2.8 3PM, 1.3 STL projected). Early in the season, check his minutes, how he handles back-to-backs, his efficiency and the Q (Ankle) status. Remember that his playoff schedule is only 3-4-3 games.
